Yes. Everything works offline. Changes sync the next time your device reaches iCloud.
How do I delete a habit or my data?

Swipe a habit to delete it, or open it and tap the delete option. This removes the habit and its history. To remove synced copies entirely, manage Quackbit in your device’s iCloud settings or at icloud.com.
Reminders are local notifications. Check that notifications are allowed for Quackbit in Settings, and that the habit repeats on that day and is not already completed.
iPhone, iPad, and Mac. There is also a separate Android app.
privacy: Quackbit is built to keep your information to yourself. There is no account, no sign-in, no advertising, and no analytics.
Quackbit collects no data. Your habits live on your devices and sync through your own private iCloud.
policy: Nothing. Quackbit does not collect, transmit, or sell any personal data. We do not run servers that receive your habits, and there is no third-party analytics or tracking SDK in the app.

The habits you create and the progress you log are stored on your device. If iCloud is available and you leave sync on, that data is also stored in your private iCloud database (Apple CloudKit), tied to your Apple ID and governed by Apple’s privacy policy. We have no ability to read it.

If you add a reminder, Quackbit asks for permission and schedules a local notification on your device. Reminders are scheduled and delivered by the system; no reminder data leaves your device for that purpose.
Home Screen and desktop widgets read the same on-device data as the app, through a shared container on your device.

If you have opted in to share diagnostics with Apple, Apple may provide us aggregate, anonymized crash reports through App Store Connect. These are controlled by your device settings, not by Quackbit.
Quackbit is not directed at children and collects no data from anyone, including children.
You can delete any habit and its history inside the app. Deleting the app removes its local data. To remove synced copies, manage Quackbit’s iCloud data in your device’s settings or at icloud.com.
If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted here with a new date. Because the app collects no data, we do not expect meaningful changes.
